Rashi on Gittin 17b:10:1.hebrew: גזייה לזמן ויהביה ניהלה - לאחר שכתב בו זמן, חתכו כדי לחפות על בת אחותו או למכור בפירות, ויהביה ניהלה, ואמרי' דגט שאין בו זמן, אם ניסת הולד כשר, וכשמוציאתו הרי היא בחזקת מגורשת ולא מיקטלה — מה הועילו חכמים בתקנתן:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:10:1.english: He cut out its date and gave it to her - After he wrote a date in it, he cut it off in order to cover up for his sister's daughter or to sell [her] produce, and gave it to her; and we say that [regarding] a bill of divorce that has no date in it, if she remarried, the child is legitimate, and when she produces it, she is presumed divorced and is not executed — what did the Sages accomplish with their enactment?

Rashi on Gittin 17b:10:2.hebrew: לרמאי לא חיישינן - לרמאות כזה, שהוא ניכר ונגלה, לא עבידי אינשי דעבדי, ולא חשו רבנן להכי:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:10:2.english: We are not concerned about a deceiver - Deceit such as this, which is recognizable and exposed, people do not typically practice, and the Sages were not concerned about this:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:11:1.hebrew: כתוב בו - זמנו בשבוע פלונית של יובל ולא כתב איזו שנה; או כתב שנה ולא כתב חדש; או כתב חדש ולא כתב שבת; או כתב שבת ולא כתב יום — מאי:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:11:1.english: Written in it - [i.e.,] its date [was written as being] in such-and-such Sabbatical cycle of the Jubilee, and he did not write which year; or he wrote the year and did not write the month; or he wrote the month and did not write the week; or he wrote the week and did not write the day — what [is the law]?

Rashi on Gittin 17b:11:2.english: He said to him: [It is] valid - [even] ab initio:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:11:3.english: What did the Sages accomplish with their ordinance - For they will not refrain from writing it [this way] for him.

Rashi on Gittin 17b:12:1.english: For the seven-year period before it - [meaning] that if she committed adultery [then], she is executed:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:12:2.hebrew: ולשבוע דבתריה - לפירות, שאם ימכור בהם, תוציא גיטה ותגבם. ואי אפשר לפרש דלשבוע דקמיה אהני לפירות, שלא תטרפם מלקוחות, דבלאו זמן נמי לא טרפה, דידה על התחתונה עד דמייתה ראיה דבתר גירושין זבין. ולשבוע דבתרא לא מהני לזנות, דלא תיקטול, דבלאו זמן נמי לא מיקטלה, דספק נפשות להקל:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:12:2.english: And for the seven-year period after it - [This is effective] regarding produce: if he sells [produce] during it, she produces her bill of divorce and collects them. And it is impossible to explain that for the seven-year period before it, it is effective regarding produce — so that she cannot seize them from buyers — because even without a date she would not seize [them], since she has the lower hand until she brings proof that he sold [them] after the divorce. And for the seven-year period after it, it is not needed regarding adultery — so that she should not be executed — because even without a date she would not be executed, since in a case of doubt regarding capital punishment, [we rule] leniently:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:1:1.english: It is not common - and the Rabbis were not concerned about it:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:2:1.hebrew: עד שעת נתינה - הלכך, זמן כתיבת גט לא מהני מידי, דכי אתיא למיטרף בעיא לאתויי סהדי אימת מטא גיטא לידה:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:2:1.english: Until the time of giving - Therefore, the date of writing a *get* [bill of divorce] is of no avail at all, for when she comes to collect [the produce], she must bring witnesses [to testify] when the *get* reached her hand:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:3:1.hebrew: משום הכי מכשר ר' שמעון - בגט מוקדם, כדאמר לקמן: קסבר ר' שמעון, כיון שנתן עיניו לגרשה, שוב אין לו פירות; הלכך, אם אתיא למיטרף לקוחות דפירות מיום כתיבה, שפיר עבדא, וטעמא דרבנן לקמיה מפרש:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:3:1.english: Due to that, Rabbi Shimon deems [it] valid - in [the case of] a predated bill of divorce, as [the Gemara] says below: Rabbi Shimon holds [that] once he set his eyes upon divorcing her, he no longer has [rights to the] produce; therefore, if she comes to seize [from] buyers of produce from the day of writing, she acts properly, and the reason of the Rabbis [the Gemara] explains later:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:3:2.english: However, according to Rabbi Yochanan - who said [that] the date was instituted because of his sister's daughter:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:3:3.hebrew: מאי טעמא דרבי שמעון דמכשיר - הא זמנין דזנאי באותו יום ועודנה אשת איש, דכל זמן שלא נחתם לא ניתן לה, וכשמעידין על זנותה מוציאה גיטה וכתוב בו מאותו יום, ואומרת: "גרושה הייתי":
Rashi on Gittin 17b:3:3.english: What is the reason that Rabbi Shimon deems [it] valid? - Surely there are times when she commits adultery on that day while she is still a married woman, for as long as it has not been signed, it has not been given to her; and when [witnesses] testify about her adultery, she produces her bill of divorce, in which [a date] from that day is written, and says, "I was [already] divorced":

Rashi on Gittin 17b:4:1.hebrew: אליבא דר' שמעון לא קאמינא - דלר"ש ודאי זמן לאו משום בת אחותו איתקן, אלא משום פירות:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:4:1.english: I am not speaking in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - For according to Rabbi Shimon, certainly [the requirement of writing] the date [in a bill of divorce] was not instituted because of [the concern about] his sister's daughter, rather because of [the husband's rights to] produce:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:4:2.hebrew: אליבא דרבנן - דמשום הכי פסלי רבנן, דקא סברי זמן משום בת אחותו:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:4:2.english: In accordance with [the opinion of] the Rabbis - for this is why the Rabbis disqualify [a bill of divorce signed at night], because they hold [that the requirement of] a date is because of [the concern about] his sister's daughter:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:5:1.hebrew: בשלמא לר' יוחנן - דאמר לרבנן משום בת אחותו, ולר' שמעון משום פירות:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:5:1.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yochanan - who said [that] according to the Rabbis [it is] because of his sister's daughter, and according to Rabbi Shimon [it is] because of produce:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:5:2.hebrew: היינו דאיכא בין רבי שמעון לרבנן - טעמא דפלוגתייהו בהכי: לרבנן פסול גט מוקדם משום בת אחותו, ולר"ש כשר, דקסבר זמן משום פירות איתקן, והלכך גט מוקדם כשר, דאי טרפא משעת כתיבה, שפיר טרפא, דהא נתן עיניו לגרשה:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:5:2.english: This is [the difference] between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis - The reason for their dispute is in this [matter]: according to the Rabbis, a predated get [bill of divorce] is invalid because of [the concern about] his sister's daughter; whereas according to Rabbi Shimon, it is valid, because he holds [that] the date was instituted on account of [the husband's rights to] produce, and therefore a predated get is valid, since if she collects [produce] from the time of writing, she collects [it] properly, as he had [already] set his eyes on divorcing her:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:5:3.hebrew: מאי איכא - במאי פליגי, ואמאי פסלי רבנן? הא שפיר טרפא, דהא להכי איתקן זמן:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:5:3.english: What [difference] is there - On what do they disagree, and why do the Rabbis invalidate [such a bill of divorce]? Surely she properly collects [the produce], since it was for this [purpose] that the date was instituted:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:6:1.hebrew: עד שעת חתימה - דלרבנן לא בעיא למיטרף אלא מחתימה ואילך, הלכך מוקדם פסול, דכי מפקא ליה אתיא למיטרף מיום כתיבה, דסברי בו ביום נחתם:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:6:1.english: Until the time of signing - For according to the Rabbis, she may only seize [produce] from [the time of] signing onward; therefore, a predated [bill of divorce] is invalid, because when she produces it, she will come to seize [produce] from the day of writing, as they assume it was signed on that very day:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:7:1.english: We heard them - [referring] to Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:9:1.hebrew: ג' גיטין פסולין - ואחד מהם יש עליו עדים ואין בו זמן, ותנן דאם ניסת הולד כשר, כיון דאי עבד שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:9:1.english: Three bills of divorce are invalid - And one of them has witnesses on it, yet has no date, and it is taught in the Mishnah that if she married [on its basis], the child is of unflawed lineage — [that is,] since if one did it [after the fact] it is valid, [what did the Sages accomplish?]:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:9:2.english: What did the Sages accomplish with their ordinance - [which they instituted] on account of his sister's daughter and on account of [the] produce:

Rashi on Gittin 17b:9:3.hebrew: אהנו דלכתחילה לא תינשא - וכיון דהכי הוא, אי בעי לכתוב גט בלא זמן לחפות על בת אחותו או למכור בפירות, לא כתבו ליה סופרי הדיינים ולא חתמי עליה סהדי:
Rashi on Gittin 17b:9:3.english: It is effective [in] that she may not marry ab initio - And since this is so, if he wants to write a bill of divorce without a date to cover up for his sister's daughter or to sell the produce, the scribes of the judges will not write [it] for him, and witnesses will not sign on it:

Tosafot on Gittin 17b:10:1.hebrew: גזייה לזמן ויהביה ניהלה מאי כו' - והא דאמר בפרק ד' אחין (יבמות לא:) גבי: "מפני מה לא תיקנו זמן בקידושין? משום דהיכי נעביד, נינחיה גבי דידה — מחקה ליה", ופריך: "אי הכי, גירושין נמי נימא הכי", ומשני: "התם להצלה דידה קאתי" — לא כמו שפירש שם בקונט', דאי מחקה ליה קטלינן לה, דמוקמינן לה בחזקת אשת איש, אע"ג דאי לא תיקון זמן מצי לחפויי עלה, דמספיקא לא קטלינן לה; השתא דתיקון זמן, אי מחקה ליה, מוקמינן לה בחזקת אשת איש וקטלינן לה. דהא הכא משמע דאי גזייה לזמן לא קטלינן לה, דקאמר: "מה הועילו חכמים בתקנתם?" ודוחק לומר דלא פריך הכא אלא למאן דאמר משום פירי. אלא אומר ר"י דהכי פירושו: התם להצלה דידה קאתי — הגט בא להצילה ולהעיד עליה שהיא מגורשת, ולכך יראה למחוק הזמן, כי סבורה שיפסול בכך; אבל האמת דאי מחקה ליה לא קטלינן לה. הכא לחובה דידה קאתי — כלומר, הקידושין באין לחייבה ולהעיד שהיא מקודשת, ומחקה ליה לזמן:
Tosafot on Gittin 17b:10:1.english: If he cut out the date and gave it to her, what [is the law], etc. - And as for that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin (Yevamot 31b) regarding: "Why did they not institute a date in [a document of] betrothal? Because how should we do [it]? Should we leave it with her? She will erase it," and it asks: "If so, [regarding] divorce as well, let us say the same [thing]!" and it answers: "There it comes for her rescue" — [this is] not as [Rashi] explained there in the commentary, that if she erases it we execute her, because we establish her in the presumptive status of a married woman; [for] even though if they had not instituted a date [her relative] could cover up for her, since out of doubt we would not execute her, now that they instituted a date, if she erases it, we establish her in the presumptive status of a married woman and execute her. For here it is implied that if he cut out the date we do not execute her, as [the Gemara] says: "What did the Sages accomplish with their enactment?" And it is forced to say that [the Gemara] only asks here according to the one who says [the date was instituted] because of produce. Rather, Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that this is its explanation: "There it comes for her rescue" — the bill of divorce comes to rescue her and to testify about her that she is divorced, and therefore she is afraid to erase the date, because she thinks that it will be invalidated thereby; but in truth, if she erases it, we do not execute her. "Here it comes to her detriment" — that is to say, the [document of] betrothal comes to obligate her and to testify that she is betrothed, and [therefore] she will erase the date:

Tosafot on Gittin 17b:13:1.hebrew: כתביה ואנחיה כו' - הכא לא בעי לשנויי דאהני לקמיה כדאמרינן לעיל; דגבי כתב חדש שבת, כיון דאהני לקמיה לא חיישי' לחפויי, שהכתיבה והנתינה כי הדדי נינהו, כמו ביומא גופא, כדאמרינן לעיל. אבל גבי כתב ואנחיה בכיסתיה, וגיטין הבאין ממ"ה, שהנתינה היא אחר הכתיבה, חיישי' שמא יחפה ויאמר שקר שמקודם לכן נתגרשה. וכן נכתב ביום ונחתם בלילה פסול, אע"ג דאהני לקמיה:
Tosafot on Gittin 17b:13:1.english: If he writes it and puts it away, etc. - Here [the Gemara] does not want to answer that it is effective for the future, as we said above; for with respect to [one who] writes [only] the month [or] week, since it is effective for the future, we are not concerned about covering up, because the writing and the giving are together, just like on the day itself, as we said above. However, with respect to [one who] writes [a bill of divorce] and puts it in his pocket, and bills of divorce that come from overseas, where the giving is after the writing, we are concerned lest he cover up [for her] and tell a lie that she was divorced earlier than that. And similarly, [a bill of divorce] written by day and signed at night is invalid, even though it is effective for the future:

Tosafot on Gittin 17b:1:1.hebrew: זנות לא שכיחא - פירוש: זנות בעדים ובהתראה לא שכיח, אבל לא בעי למימר דשום זנות לא שכיח; דהא בריש כתובות (דף ב.) תקנו שתהא בתולה נישאת ביום הרביעי, שאם היה לו טענת בתולים ישכים לבית דין, דחיישינן לאיקרורי דעתא, ומסתברא דטפי איכא למיחש לשמא תזנה מלשמא זנתה. ועוד, דהתם אע"ג דלא שכיח עשו תקנה וחשו שלא תאסר עליו עולמית ויתפסנה באיסור; אבל הכא לא חשו אי מחייבת מיתה ולא מיקטלה, כיון דלא שכיח:
Tosafot on Gittin 17b:1:1.english: Adultery is infrequent - Meaning: adultery with witnesses and forewarning is infrequent, but [the Gemara] does not mean to say that no adultery at all is frequent; for at the beginning of Ketubot (2a) they instituted that a virgin is married on Wednesday, so that if [the husband] has a claim concerning [her] virginity he will go early to court, because we are concerned about his anger cooling down, and it is reasonable that there is more reason to be concerned about "perhaps she will commit adultery" than "perhaps she committed adultery." Furthermore, there, even though it is infrequent, they made an enactment and were concerned lest she become forbidden to him forever and he retain her in [a state of] prohibition; whereas here, they were not concerned if she is liable to the death penalty and is not executed, since it is infrequent:

Tosafot on Gittin 17b:2:1.hebrew: עד שעת נתינה - פי' בקונט': הלכך זמן כתיבת הגט לא מהני, דכי בעיא למיטרף, בעיא לאיתויי סהדי אימת מטא גיטא לידה. אע"ג דבכל שטרות אין צריך להביא עדים אימת מטא השטר לידיה, אפי' למאן דלית ליה "עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו", היינו משום דלדידיה אין כותבין שטר ללוה אלא א"כ מלוה עמו, בר משטרי אקנייתא, כדאמרי' בפ"ק דב"מ (דף יג.); הלכך כיון שהיה מלוה שם, אמרי' שמיד מסר לו. אבל גט אשה כותבין לאיש אע"פ שאין אשתו עמו, משום עיגונא, כמו כל גיטין הבאין ממדינת הים. אבל קשה לר"י מהא דאמר בסוף פ"ק דב"מ (דף יט.): מצא גט אשה בשוק, בזמן שהבעל מודה יחזיר לאשה; ופריך: ניחוש דלמא כתב ליתן בניסן ולא נתן עד תשרי, ואזל וזבן פירי מניסן עד תשרי, ומפקא ליה לגיטא דכתב בניסן ואתיא למטרף לקוחות שלא כדין! ומשני: כי אתיא למטרף, אמרי' לה אייתי ראייה אימת מטא גיטא לידך. ואמאי קשה ליה טפי אההיא ברייתא מבכל גיטין שבעולם? אלא משמע דוקא בגט הנמצא, דאיתרע בנפילה, הוא דאמר "אייתי ראיה אימת מטא גיטא לידך", אבל בכל גיטין אמרינן מסתמא ביום שנכתב ונחתם נמסר! ואומר ר"י דהכי פירושו: "עד שעת נתינה" — דכיון דיש לבעל פירות עד שעת נתינה, לא הוצרכו לתקן זמן בגט משום פירות, דבאין בו זמן נמי תביא גיטה לב"ד או לעדים, ויכתבו לה שמאותו יום נתגרשה. וא"ת: ולר' יוחנן, היאך כותבין גט לאיש אע"פ שאין אשתו עמו? ניחוש שמא יכתוב בניסן ולא יתן עד תשרי, כדפרי' בפ"ק דב"מ (דף יב:) גבי כותבין שטר ללוה אע"פ שאין מלוה עמו! וי"ל דגבי כותבין שטר ללוה פריך, משום דמאן דיזיף בצנעה יזיף, ויש לחוש שאחר זמן ימסור לו בצנעה, ויסברו לקוחות שנמסר לו משעת כתיבה. אבל גט צריך עדי מסירה — ואפי' לר' מאיר [דאמר עדי חתימה כרתי] אומר ר"ת דבעינן עדי מסירה, דאין דבר שבערוה פחות משנים — וגם מפרסמין להוציא קול שהיא פנויה, וידעו לקוחות שלא נתגרשה מיום הכתיבה, ויאמרו לה "אייתי ראיה אימת" כו'. ומיהו במשליש גט לאשתו דשמעתין ליכא למיחש לרבי יוחנן למידי, לא משום פירות ולא משום שמא יחפה, דכיון שרואים זמן הכתיבה קודם המסירה, קלא אית ליה, כדאמר בסמוך אגיטין הבאין ממדינת הים. וא"ת: נכתב ביום ונחתם בלילה אמאי פסול, הא אית ליה קלא? וי"ל דלא שייך למימר "קלא אית ליה" אלא כשמגרש ע"י שליח, אבל נכתב ביום ונחתם בלילה יש לחוש שימסור לה בעצמו בצנעה לחפות עליה; ולהכי לא מצי לשנויי גבי "כתביה ואותביה בכיסתיה" דקלא אית ליה, כדמשני אגיטין הבאין ממדינת הים. וא"ת: ואמאי כותבין גט לאיש, ליחוש שמא תזנה ויתן לה בצנעה כדי לחפות עליה? וי"ל דמסתמא מיד אחר הכתיבה יתן לה, דלא מקדים פורענותא לנפשיה, כדמשני בסמוך גבי "כתביה ואותביה בכיסתיה":
Tosafot on Gittin 17b:2:1.english: Until the time of giving - Rashi explained: Therefore, the date of the writing of the bill of divorce is of no avail, for when she wants to seize [produce sold by her husband], she must bring witnesses [as to] when the bill of divorce reached her hand. Even though in [the case of] all [other] documents one does not need to bring witnesses [as to] when the document reached his hand — even according to the one who does not hold "its witnesses in its signatures acquire for him" — that is because according to him, one does not write a document for a borrower unless the lender is with him, apart from deeds of transfer (aknayata), as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (13a); therefore, since the lender was there, we say that he handed it over to him immediately. However, a woman's bill of divorce may be written for a man even though his wife is not with him, because of [the concern of leaving her] an agunah [unable to remarry], like all bills of divorce that come from overseas. However, it is difficult for Rabbeinu Yitzchak from that which [the Gemara] says at the end of the first chapter of Bava Metzia (19a): [If] one found a woman's bill of divorce in the marketplace, when the husband admits [it is valid], he returns [it] to the woman; and [the Gemara] asks: Let us be concerned lest he wrote [it] to give in Nisan and did not give [it] until Tishrei, and he went and sold produce from Nisan until Tishrei, and she produces the bill of divorce that was written in Nisan and comes to seize [from] buyers unlawfully! And [the Gemara] answers: When she comes to seize, we say to her, "Bring proof [as to] when the bill of divorce reached your hand." Now why was it more difficult for [the Gemara] regarding that baraita than regarding all bills of divorce in the world? Rather, it implies [that] specifically in [the case of] a found bill of divorce, which has been impaired by having fallen, is where [the Gemara] said, "Bring proof [as to] when the bill of divorce reached your hand," whereas in all [ordinary] bills of divorce we say [that] presumably it was handed over on the day it was written and signed! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that this is its explanation: "Until the time of giving" — since the husband has [the rights to the] produce until the time of giving, they did not need to institute a date in a bill of divorce on account of produce; for even with [a bill of divorce] that has no date in it, she will bring her bill of divorce to the court or to witnesses, and they will write for her that she was divorced from that day. And if you ask: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, how may we write a bill of divorce for a man even though his wife is not with him? Let us be concerned lest he write [it] in Nisan and not give [it] until Tishrei, as [the Gemara] asks in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (12b) regarding writing a document for a borrower even though the lender is not with him! And one can answer that regarding writing a document for a borrower [the Gemara] asks [this], because one who borrows does so in private, and there is [reason] to be concerned that after some time he will hand [it] over to him in private, and buyers will think that it was handed over to him from the time of writing. However, a bill of divorce requires witnesses to the delivery — and even according to Rabbi Meir [who says the witnesses to the signing effect the divorce], Rabbeinu Tam says that we require witnesses to the delivery, because no matter of marital status [can be established with] fewer than two [witnesses] — and furthermore they publicize [it] to spread a report that she is unmarried, so buyers will know that she was not divorced from the day of writing, and they will say to her, "Bring proof when [it reached your hand]," etc. However, in [the case of] one who deposits a bill of divorce with a third party for his wife, which is our sugya, there is nothing to be concerned about according to Rabbi Yoḥanan — neither on account of produce nor on account of "lest he cover up [for her]" — because since they see the date of writing [is] prior to the delivery, it has publicity, as [the Gemara] says shortly below regarding bills of divorce that come from overseas. And if you ask: [If a bill of divorce] was written by day and signed at night, why is it invalid? Surely it has publicity! And one can answer that it is not relevant to say "it has publicity" except when he divorces through an agent; however, [when it is] written by day and signed at night, there is [reason] to be concerned that he will hand [it] over to her himself in private in order to cover up for her. And for this reason [the Gemara] could not answer regarding "he wrote it and put it in his pocket" that it has publicity, as it answers regarding bills of divorce that come from overseas. And if you ask: Why do we write a bill of divorce for a man [when his wife is not present]? Let us be concerned lest she commit adultery and he give [it] to her in private in order to cover up for her! And one can answer that presumably he will give [it] to her immediately after the writing, because a person does not bring misfortune upon himself prematurely, as [the Gemara] answers shortly below regarding "he wrote it and put it in his pocket":
